full_judgment:
4. It is very pertinent to mention hear that the plaintiff bank instituted the suit for realization of Taka 2,05,16,249.88, as per the bank statement up to 31-8-1992. In Paragraph 12 of the plaint the details statement of 27 LIM account had been mentioned and in paragraphs 13 and 15 of the plaint aforesaid amount was mentioned, but it appears from the records that subsequently in paragraph 12 of the plaint a correction was made, having no initial of the learned trial Judge or concern officer of the Courts below and the figure of total dues was corrected as Taka 2,05,20,049 and in paragraph 13, 15 and prayer portion of the plaint the total dues had been corrected by red ink as Taka 1,59,00,049.88 by pen through. The claim of the plaintiff bank mentioned in paragraph 12 are quite different and inconsistent with the amount mentioned in paragraphs 13, 15 and in the prayer portion of the plaint. We along with the learned Advocate of the plaintiff appellant have checked up the lower Court record. But we found that in changing/amending/correcting the total dues/amount of the plaintiff bank in paragraphs 12, 13, 15 and prayer portion, there is no official endorsement on it by the court's below. Even the learned Advocate of the plaintiff-appellant failed to satisfy us on this point that at whose instance and how the Courts document was corrected/amended or penning through without any court's order, having no official endorsement. It creates doubt in our mind whether it was a bona fide mistake of the learned trial Court or it was a manipulated job by the plaintiff bank. We also do not find any application for amendment of the paint to that effect in the lower Court record. 

 7. The plaintiffs to prove its claim examined only one witness and adduced documentary evidence which were marked as exhibit Nos. 1-14. On the other hand the defendant No.3 examined himself to prove his case. The learned Subordinate Judge and Artha Rin Adalat after hearing the suit by its judgment and decree dated 24-3-1998 decreed the suit in part for an amount of Taka 34,07,104.30 instead of Taka 2,05,16,249.00 or Taka 1,59,00,049.88 (if we accept the correction/ amendment of the plaint). 

 13. Mr Bayejid, learned Advocate of the appellant failed to show us with reference to the evidence and materials on record that in arriving at the above findings the learned Subordinate Judge and Artha Rin Adalat misread and misconstrued any evidence and materials on record. 

 14. In course of argument when we asked the learned Advocate of the appellant to provide information about the latest position of 14 Pickup Vans, which not sold before filling of the suit, then the learned Advocate by filling a supplementary paper book submitted two documents marking as annexures-X and XI. From the said documents it also appears that before instituting the suit 13 Pickup Vans were sold at Taka 58,61,152.00. It also appears from the record that PW-1 was examined before the Court on 7-2-1994 and before that rest 14 Pickup Vans, which were under the custody of the plaintiff were sold at Taka 46,20,000.00, despite the PW-1 in his deposition did not say anything about the sell of the 14 Pickup Vans after institution of the suit. It also appears from annexure-X that 10 Pickup Vans were sold by the plaintiff bank at the rate of Taka 3,00,000 where it is very much clear from exhibits-11 and 13 and deposition of DW-1 that the defendants offered Taka 3,50,000 to the plaintiff bank to get delivery of each Pickup Van and also promised that they would pay the shortfall amount, if any. From annexure-XI it appears that 14 Pickup Vans were sold at Taka 46,20,000. But from exhibit-14, the bank statement, it appears that the said money was never adjusted against the LIM accounts. Even said fact had not been brought at any stage before the trial Court. 

 Send down the lower Court records at once.
